content_voiceover: This slide covers part one of the International Consensus Classification, or ICC, approach to MDS, and it is also a favorite exam topic. The ICC groups T P 53 mutated myeloid neoplasms along a blast count spectrum. MDS with mutated T P 53 requires any degree of cytopenia and 0 to 9 percent blasts in marrow or blood, with either a multi hit T P 53 mutation, or a single T P 53 mutation with variant allele frequency above 10 percent occurring alongside a complex karyotype that often shows loss of 17 p. MDS slash AML with mutated T P 53 uses the same any cytopenia requirement but blasts rise to 10 to 19 percent, and here any somatic T P 53 mutation with variant allele frequency above 10 percent qualifies, without needing the multi hit criterion or complex karyotype. AML with mutated T P 53 does not require cytopenia at all, requires blasts of 20 percent or more, and again just needs any somatic T P 53 mutation above 10 percent variant allele frequency. The slide then defines multi hit T P 53 mutations precisely. This means either two distinct T P 53 mutations each with variant allele frequency above 10 percent, or a single T P 53 mutation combined with a 17 p deletion on cytogenetics, a variant allele frequency above 50 percent, or copy neutral loss of heterozygosity at the 17 p T P 53 locus. The superscript note clarifies that complex karyotype with loss of 17 p is used as a proxy when T P 53 locus loss of heterozygosity information is not available.
keypoints: T P 53 mutated disease forms a continuum by blast percentage under ICC
0 to 9 percent blasts needs multi hit T P 53 or high V A F plus complex karyotype
10 to 19 percent blasts, called MDS slash AML, needs only any T P 53 mutation above 10 percent V A F
20 percent or more blasts is AML with mutated T P 53, cytopenia not required
Multi hit definition: two mutations, or one mutation plus 17p deletion, high V A F, or c n L O H
keypoint_voiceover: The exam pearl here is that as blast percentage rises, the genetic bar for calling T P 53 mutated disease actually gets lower. Below 10 percent blasts you need the strict multi hit definition or a high variant allele frequency plus complex karyotype. Once blasts reach 10 percent, any somatic T P 53 mutation above 10 percent variant allele frequency is sufficient, whether it is called MDS slash AML or frank AML with mutated T P 53.
